transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that... I keep having these moments where things just feel off. My own house or my office will suddenly feel completely unreal to me. It's hard to explain, but it's almost like... like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there in my own body. It's been bothering me enough that I thought I should come in and talk to someone about it.
Do you find that you spend a significant amount of your time feeling excessively worried or anxious about a wide range of different things, such as your job, health, or daily responsibilities?

No, not really. I mean, I'm a tax preparer, so there's always some stress around deadlines, but I wouldn't say I'm excessively worried about everything. It's not my job or my health or just daily chores that are bothering me. It's really just those weird moments I mentioned, where things just don't feel real.
Have you ever experienced any significant traumatic events or abuse in your past?
No, I haven't. Honestly, I've had a pretty normal life. There wasn't any abuse or... or big traumatic events in my past or anything like that.
When you have these moments where things feel unreal, do you also feel as though your own emotions are detached or muted, almost like you are an outside observer of your own feelings?

No, I wouldn't say my emotions feel muted or detached like that. When it happens, I still feel... well, I feel confused and unsettled by it, mostly. But I don't feel like an outside observer of my own feelings, just of my body or my surroundings. My emotions still feel like my own.
During these moments, do you ever feel like you have lost track of time or have gaps in your memory where you aren't sure what you were doing?

Well, not exactly in a general sense, but... there is one specific gap that bothers me. When that client got aggressive... I remember him crowding me in my office, getting right up in my space. And I remember the police being there later. But the middle part—like, what he actually said right before I reached for the phone to call for help—is just a blank. No matter how hard I try to pull it up, I just can't remember it. It's just gone.

Are these experiences of feeling like you are watching yourself from outside your body something that happens only when you think about that specific incident with your client, or do they happen at other times when you are not thinking about that event?

Well, I haven't really noticed it happening at other times. It pretty much just hits me when my mind goes back to that day in the office with the client. If I'm doing something else and not thinking about what happened, I don't get that... that weird outside-my-body feeling. It just seems tied to the incident.
How long ago did this incident with the client take place?
It's been about two weeks now. Yeah, all of this started right after he threatened me in my office.
